main_text.p: difficillimum illud, Memoria in mendace; eludit.Si quis enim Iaponicas & Indicas illorum epistolas scrutari velit, nihil praeter rudem agrestemque Idololatriam, superstitionem, & tyrannidem Antichristi, ab ipsis sub Christi nomine, induci comperiet. Historiam contexere non statui, causas autem, cur tam sterile ipsorum semen sit in agro Indico, annotare propositum est, inter quas imaginum cultus praecipuus est, qui homines ab interna & spirituali Dei adoratione, ad externas nænias, Deoque exosas & hominibus perniciosas nugas avocat:quam abominationem quo studio excolant, quove fuco Ethnicis proponant, uno addito exemplo docebo. Iesuita Pime-rus in epist. ex urbe cam-baja.Sa-cellum erat inquit Iesuita Pimerus, multis rosis odoriferis, elegantissimisque floribus ita exornatum ut cœlum quoddam esse videretur: omnibus hisce diebus a lusitanis tanto studio frequentabat, ac si consequendi Iubilæi spem habuissent: & idem faciebant omnes gentiles & Mauri, intran-tesque dicebant se divini quid persenti-scere; & attoniti addebant, An Deus hic est? num hic habitat? multi quoque procedebant in genua, ad adorandum puerum Iesum, & ejus pedes osculabantur, turbini-bus suis e capite depositis. page.notes: The first paragraph continues from the previous page. The repeated opening quotation marks at the start of each line (from "videretur" to "scere") are printed as one quotation and are given once here. "eludit.Si" is printed without a space. "cœlum" is read as printed, not fully certain. The apostrophe-like mark in "agro Indico" is printed as a small stroke and is not transcribed. The catchword "bant" completes "præstabant". The left margin note is set in italic and is partly faded at the line ends. Faint show-through of the reverse side is visible and is not transcribed.
